# Use exam-paper-check

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Check an exam paper and its mark scheme before they go to print or to a moderator — a script reads the teacher's own files and finds part marks that don't add up to a question's total, questions that don't add up to the paper's total (an either/or choice counted once), numbering that skips or repeats, parts with no marks, parts the mark scheme misses or marks differently, and objectives that are never assessed or far off their weighting — then reads the questions for clarity and fairness.

**Reach for it when** a teacher asks to "check my exam paper", "proofread this test", "does the mark scheme match the paper", "do the marks add up", "check this assessment before moderation", or "is this paper balanced across the objectives".

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install exam-paper-check                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install exam-paper-check --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install exam-paper-check --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Educator pack: [`--pack educator`](../packs/use-the-educator-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/educator/skills/exam-paper-check/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Check my exam paper before it goes to print"
- "Does the mark scheme match the paper?"
- "Do the marks on this test add up?"
- "Check this assessment is balanced across AO1 to AO3 before moderation"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Write ten multiple-choice questions on photosynthesis"
- "Make a slide deck for my Year 9 lesson on forces"
- "Proofread this research paper's citations"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use exam-paper-check".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every total is added from the files,** and every mismatch names the question and part.
- **The mark scheme is lined up against the paper part by part,** both ways.
- **An either/or choice counts once,** and its two options must be worth the same.
- **The reply leads with what to fix before printing,** in plain words, with no mention of scripts or files.
- **Fixes are the smallest that work,** with the assumption stated when it's unclear which number is wrong.
- **Their files are never overwritten,** and every change in a corrected copy is listed.

## Use something else when

- Writing questions or a paper from scratch: write it, then check it here
- Marking students' scripts or moderating their marks
- Setting grade boundaries
- Coursework or essays with no marks per part
